minutes.headline: Commission voted to issue an enforcement order for wetlands violations on Massachusetts Avenue
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission held several new and continued wetland hearings (additions, a boat ramp, common driveways, a wetland crossing), most of which were continued to July 15th pending DEP file numbers or further plans. The commission also voted to issue an enforcement order against a Massachusetts Avenue property for unpermitted wetland alteration, approved a three-year extension for the Chase Road auto dealership redevelopment after discussing an unpermitted car-washing/discharge issue, and committed timber rights funds toward a Forest Legacy land-preservation deal.

public_comment.topic: Raised concerns about stormwater/boat-wash runoff from the proposed Reservoir Recreational Trust boat ramp and suggested a permeable ramp surface instead of solid concrete.

budget_items.topic: Mass Recreational Trails grant applications (Table Rock parking area and Reo property park)
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission was notified that neither of its two trail grant applications was funded this cycle; overall program funding was reported as down, with only a fraction of applications funded this year.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the timber rights fund had been holding money in reserve for a 25% grant match that is no longer needed since the trail grants were not awarded, freeing it for the Massie tract cost share.

what_happened.line: Commission voted 4-0 to issue an enforcement order for unpermitted wetland alteration on a Massachusetts Avenue property, with one member recused.
Commission approved a three-year extension for the Chase Road auto dealership redevelopment after discussing an unpermitted car-washing discharge on the site.
Commission voted to use timber rights fund money to cover a share of title costs for the Massie tract Forest Legacy land purchase.
Several pending wetland hearings, including a boat ramp, common driveways, and a utility substation, were continued to July 15.

why_it_matters: The enforcement order sets a compliance deadline for a specific property's wetland violation and directs the town's response to it.
The Chase Road extension keeps a commercial redevelopment project moving while the town follows up on a stormwater discharge concern raised during review.
Committing timber rights fund money to a land purchase is a use of town conservation funds rather than a new tax cost to residents.
